ai_show_review.summary: Blazing Lovelight debut & expansive Alligator jam
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a scorching first performance of Turn On Your Lovelight followed by a marathon Alligator jam that showcases Pigpen’s vocal fire and Garcia’s searing guitar. Both tracks are high‑energy highlights with tight ensemble work throughout.
ai_show_review.review: On August 5, 1967 at Toronto's O'Keefe Center the Dead gave early‑Dead fans a taste of what was to become legendary. The night opened with an electrifying Turn On Your Lovelight – Pigpen’s raw vocals and organ riffs set the stage for a wild ride that has since been cited as the first recorded rendition of the song. Without missing a beat, they launched into Alligator, a sprawling psychedelic jam where Jerry Garcia’s guitar “tear[ed] up the place” and Bob Weir added a rich, full‑tone backdrop, while Bill Kreutzmann kept a steady, driving pulse. The two‑song set is a concise but powerful snapshot of the band’s early chemistry, captured in surprisingly clear soundboard recordings that let every nuance shine.

best_recording.reason: Excellent, well‑balanced soundboard capture with no drop‑outs; provides the clearest listening experience of both Lovelight and Alligator.

key_highlights: First recorded performance of Turn On Your Lovelight.
Expansive Alligator jam that showcases ensemble chemistry.
Pigpen’s powerful vocals and organ drive the Lovelight opening.
Crystal‑clear soundboard audio makes both tracks highly enjoyable.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is described as ‘tearing up the place’, driving the intensity of both Lovelight and Alligator with soulful, searing leads.
band_performance.Bob: Bob Weir’s tone is rich and full, adding depth to the Alligator jam and complementing Jerry’s lead work.
band_performance.Pigpen: Pigpen energizes Turn On Your Lovelight with powerful vocals, organ riffs, and harmonica flair, setting a high‑octane tone for the set.
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann provides steady, driving propulsion throughout both songs, anchoring the band’s improvisational flights.
